classification.difficultyReason: Select matching vertices and SAS/AAS tests in four explicitly supplied triangle comparisons, derive a third angle and recognise a nonmatching side. These are taught congruence applications with prompted reasons; the isosceles double ordering follows equal base angles.

content.prompt: In each part below, say whether the two triangles are congruent. If they are, write a congruence statement, including the appropriate congruence test.

spec.description: Two separate triangles in a comparison row. QR and AC carry the respective 15 mm givens. Ordinary source blue outlines are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: Triangle PQR: angle Q = 60 degrees, angle P = 50 degrees, QR = 15 mm. Triangle ABC: angle B = 60 degrees, angle A = 50 degrees, AC = 15 mm.

answer.worked: The angle correspondence is $P\leftrightarrow A$, $Q\leftrightarrow B$, $R\leftrightarrow C$, since the third angle in each triangle is $70^\circ$. Thus $QR$ corresponds to $BC$, whereas $AC$ corresponds to $PR$. The equal given lengths are not matching sides: $QR=15\text{ mm}$ is opposite $50^\circ$, while $AC=15\text{ mm}$ is opposite $60^\circ$. The triangles are not congruent.

spec.description: ABC is lower-left and QPR upper-right. Both right-angle squares are derived from the adjoining edges. Ordinary outlines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: AB = PR = 9 cm; BC = PQ = 12 cm; angle ABC = angle RPQ = 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only printed givens and right-angle marks are visible.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle RPQ$:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=RP=9\text{ cm}\\BC&=PQ=12\text{ cm}\\\angle ABC&=\angle RPQ=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The equal angles are included between the equal sides. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle RPQ$ (SAS).

spec.description: Two separate triangles remain side by side, with AB and RP carrying the length labels. Ordinary source blue outlines are reconstructed in black.
spec.mathematics: AB = RP = 6 m; angle A = 30 degrees; angle B = 110 degrees; angle Q = 40 degrees; angle R = 110 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-30^\circ-110^\circ\\\angle ACB&=40^\circ.\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PRQ$, $\angle ABC=\angle PRQ=110^\circ$, $\angle ACB=\angle PQR=40^\circ$, and the matching sides $AB=PR=6\text{ m}$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PRQ$ (AAS).

spec.description: Two separate triangles remain side by side. AC and QP carry the 8 cm labels. Ordinary outlines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: AC = QP = 8 cm; angle A = angle P = 50 degrees; angle B = angle Q = 65 degrees.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PRQ$ (AAS). Also valid: $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-50^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle ACB&=65^\circ.\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PRQ$, $\angle BAC=\angle RPQ=50^\circ$, $\angle ACB=\angle PQR=65^\circ$, and the matching sides $AC=PQ=8\text{ cm}$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PRQ$ (AAS).

Both triangles have two $65^\circ$ angles, so the corresponding equal-angle vertices may also be exchanged. Thus $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$ is also valid.
